_comment: EXAMPLE FILE. The registrations and figures below are invented and describe
no real aircraft. Do not fly on them. Copy this file to datasets/fleet.json
and replace every entry with the figures from your own aircraft.
The calculator reads datasets/fleet.json at startup and appends whatever it
finds to the aircraft list. The file is optional: without it the calculator
still works with the handbook sample aircraft and the custom aircraft, and
says so in the interface.
Per-aircraft weight and balance data, one entry per registration. These
figures belong to the individual aircraft, not to the type: POH 6.2 marks
them with an asterisk and says they 'are to be obtained from the applicable
aircraft's weight and balance manifest'. The authority is that aircraft's
own current approved documentation, usually that manifest and possibly an
approved supplement, over anything generic to the type. Record which one in
source_document. The figures change with every repaint, instrument change
and reweighing, so they are only as good as the date beside them.
FIELDS
registration    Required. Any non-empty string. Shown in the aircraft list.
type            Required. Selects the fallback CG limits and the handbook
reference. Known values:
alpha_trainer      -> POH-162-00-40-001
alpha_trainer_pro  -> POH-162-00-40-003
empty_weight    Required. Both kg and lbs, and they have to agree.
empty_arm       Required. Both mm and in, and they have to agree.
serial_number   Optional. Displayed under the aircraft list.
weighing_date   Optional but recommended. The date of the weight and
balance report these figures come from. Left null, the
interface flags the empty weight as unverifiable.
source_document Optional. Names the document these figures were taken
from, so the entry can be checked against it later. The
calculator does not read this field: it is here for the
person maintaining the file, which is the only reader who
can act on it.
cg_limits       Optional. The same authority reaches the CG limits, so
declare them here when that aircraft's documentation
states its own.
Both unit systems are required and have to agree, and the
forward limit has to sit ahead of the rearward one, or the
whole aircraft is rejected rather than half-applied. Left
null, the aircraft inherits the envelope its type publishes
and the interface says the limits are not from its manifest.
note            Optional. Free text shown with the aircraft.
An entry that fails validation is skipped and the calculator says how many it
skipped; it never falls back to a default silently. Editing this file needs
no code change.
Arms and MTOM are type data, not airframe data: they live in the calculator
and the test suite checks them against the handbooks.

aircraft.note: Invented aircraft, example only. Its own documentation states no CG limits, so it inherits the ones its type publishes.
Invented aircraft, example only. This one states its own CG limits, which win over the ones its type publishes.
